article.title: As U.S. Boycotts U.N. Climate Talks, California Leads State/City Efforts to Combat Climate Crisis
article.content: For the second year in a row, the Trump administration has not sent an official delegation to the United Nations’ annual climate change conference, held this year in Antalya, Turkey. But although no federal representatives are present, more than 120 U.S. state and local leaders are participating, including the governor of the fourth-largest economy in the world, California Governor Gavin Newsom. Newsom, a likely candidate for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, has endorsed the Santa Marta Process, a coalition of nations working to develop a global green energy transition. “The petrostates have made it abundantly clear: Under the current rules of consensus, they are never, ever going to allow COPs to succeed. They’re just not going to sign that agreement. So, essentially, the Santa Marta coalition is making an end run around that, using economic power,” says longtime environmental and climate reporter Mark Hertsgaard.
